name: Assyrian Neo-Aramaic

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Assyrian Neo-Aramaic (assy1241).

notes:
Assyrian Neo-Aramaic (Suret), a modern Semitic (Afroasiatic, Northeastern Neo-Aramaic) language written in the East Syriac abjad. The spec describes UNPOINTED East Syriac spelling: vowel quality is written by the East Syriac vowel points and consonant quality by the qushshaya and rukkakha dots and by majliana, and none of those marks are part of the letter string this spec receives. What the bare letters still decide is the matres lectionis and the word-edge behaviour of the letters that carry them.

Matres lectionis. Alaph, waw and yudh double as vowel letters, the system Nöldeke's Compendious Syriac Grammar (1904) describes in §4 for Syriac generally. Alaph is the glottal stop word-initially, where it carries an initial vowel; word-finally it is the vowel of the determined-state ending -a, and medially it is ambiguous between the glottal stop and a written long vowel, so both readings stand in the lattice with the consonant first. Waw is consonantal /w/ word-initially and otherwise writes the back rounded vowels /u uː o oː/; yudh is consonantal /j/ word-initially and otherwise writes /i iː e eː/. The ordering inside each list is a frequency claim measured on the shipped WikiPron gold, not an editorial guess: word-final alaph is a vowel in 3232 of 3236 gold sites and [ɑː] in 2314 of them; word-initial alaph is [ʔ] in 363 of 382; word-initial waw is [w] in 21 of 24 and word-initial yudh is [j] in 120 of 135.

Begadkepat. Historic postvocalic spirantization of the six plosives is fossilized rather than synchronic here, and unpointed spelling does not say which reflex a given token has, so both reflexes stand in the lattice. The qushshaya/rukkakha pointing mechanism itself, and the historical tendency of the East-Syrian (Nestorian) reading tradition to give pe a hard, non-spirantized pronunciation almost throughout, are read this session in Nöldeke §§15, 23 and support pe's exclusion from the word-final fricative set below. Which reflex leads for the other five letters in the modern spoken dialect is a claim this spec attributes to Khan (2016) and Odisho (1988); neither edition was reachable this session (Khan is paywalled at Brill and on its academia.edu mirror; no copy of Odisho was found), so it is carried here as standard in the unconsulted descriptive literature, not verified against a fetched passage. Word position does discriminate: word-finally the fricative reflex leads for beth, gamal, dalath, kaph and taw, while pe does not spirantize at all, because *p is merged into /p/ outside the Tyari, Barwari and Chaldean varieties and [f] survives mainly in loanwords. Medially the plosive leads for all six, so the letters keep their plain values there and no medial spirantization is declared.

Heth is [x] rather than [ħ] in Assyrian Neo-Aramaic, so the velar fricative leads and the pharyngeal is kept as a minority reading. Ayin is retained as /ʕ/. The affricates /t͡ʃ d͡ʒ ʒ/ are written with the majliana mark on kaph, gamal, zain and shin; since the mark is absent from unpointed text they are carried as minority readings of those letters. These four claims (heth, ayin, and the majliana affricate assignments) are the same standard-in-the-literature-but-unconsulted-this-session case as the begadkepat direction above: they are attributed to Khan (2016) and Odisho (1988), neither of which was reachable, and majliana does not appear at all in Nöldeke's 1904 grammar, which predates that reading-tradition sign's currency. Gemination, stress and the emphatic spread of the emphatic consonants are not encoded.

Doubled waw. A written ⟨ܘܘ⟩ digraph is not a doubled vowel letter. The shipped gold has 27 rows containing ⟨ܘܘ⟩, reducing to 18 unique headwords: 16 carry it non-initially (13 word-medially, 3 word-finally) and 2 open with it. Across the 16 non-initial headwords no gold reading repeats [uː], so the digraph is given its own entry, [uw] ahead of [uww], instead of resolving to the two single-waw vowel readings. That is a distributional finding measured on the shipped gold, not a claim drawn from a grammar; no citation for the convention itself is offered. The second waw is not invariably consonantal: ⟨ܓܝܘܘ⟩ reads [ɡiːwoː], with the FIRST waw consonantal and the SECOND the vowel [oː]. That headword is also the only place in the class where the digraph entry costs anything, PER 0.3333 with the two single-waw readings against 0.5000 with the digraph. It pays for itself elsewhere: ⟨ܗܘܘ⟩ falls from 1.2500 to 0.7500 and ⟨ܡܥܘܘܟܐ⟩ from 0.5556 to 0.3333. The digraph reading is confined to non-initial position. Word-initial waw is consonantal /w/, as the matres lectionis paragraph above states, so a digraph entry in the general table would outrank that rule and make the engine open a word with a vowel the spec says cannot stand there, giving [uw] for ⟨ܘܘ⟩ and [uwɑː] for ⟨ܘܘܐ⟩. The entry is therefore keyed word_initial in positional_graphemes, the same shape the single letters ⟨ܐ⟩, ⟨ܘ⟩ and ⟨ܝ⟩ already use. Word-initially ⟨ܘܘ⟩ therefore reads [wuː] or [woː], the initial consonant followed by the vowel the second waw carries, which is what the two single letters would give. The two gold entries there, [waw] and [wawwa], score the same either way (0.6667 and 0.8000), so the correction costs no PER; it removes an output the spec's own phonology forbids.

Input-limited measurements. None of the 7851 gold headwords in aii_syrc_narrow.tsv carry any Syriac combining diacritic (U+0730-U+074A, the vowel points and the qushshaya/rukkakha/majliana dots): the gold is entirely unpointed, so no rule in this spec can be handed a pointed form to disambiguate. Folding vowel QUALITY in both hypothesis and gold to one symbol per length class, keeping length distinct, moves the wikipron PER from 0.3758 to 0.3165 (measured against the harness's own scorer this session); folding gemination/length alone, leaving vowel quality distinct, gives 0.3777, i.e. no improvement. The residual after the real spec is dominated by the hypothesis OMITTING phones the gold writes, not by choosing the wrong one: the leading single-character deletions (gold character, hypothesis has nothing) measured this session are a 2244, ː 1578, ɑ 1328, ɪ 1006, ə 809, e 397, against 9402 deletions, 5021 substitutions and 493 insertions overall. Begadkepat-direction mismatches (gold spirant against a hypothesis plosive, or the reverse) total 440 (θ vs t 269, x vs k 91, ð vs d 80), an order of magnitude smaller than the deletion total and already the documented majority-reading trade-off above. The conclusion: this row is input-limited because unpointed East Syriac does not write short vowels or length, so no rule can recover a phone the letters never encode. A vowel-quality fold is therefore the wrong instrument for this gold — it scores a phonemic contrast the spelling cannot carry — and a consonant-only floor is the right one, since the errors are omissions of unwritten material, not wrong choices among written alternatives. valid_ceiling is deliberately left unset: issue #1350 records that field as language-scoped while this measurement is dataset-scoped, and the two have not been reconciled.

sources.title: The Neo-Aramaic Dialect of the Assyrian Christians of Urmi
sources.notes: Standard reference grammar for the Christian Urmi dialect underlying the Iraqi Koine; cited for the phonology of the variety as a whole. Fetch was attempted for this spec (Brill's own page and the academia.edu mirror of vol. 1, Phonology and Morphology) and both refused access without payment or login, so the edition remains not consulted and no locator is claimed. The modern-dialect claims this spec would otherwise attribute to Khan (heth realized [x], the majliana affricate assignments, the *p merger outside Tyari/Barwari/Chaldean) are marked in the notes as resting on this unconsulted literature rather than on a verified passage.

sources.author: Nöldeke, Theodor (trans. Crichton, James A.)
sources.title: Compendious Syriac Grammar
sources.notes: Fetched and read this session (Internet Archive OCR text). Section 4 (pp. 5-6) is read for the matres lectionis system itself: 'The letters [alaph, waw, yudh] are frequently made use of by the Syrians to express vowel sounds' — alaph for a/e, waw for u/o and the diphthongs, yudh for i/e; this supports that the three letters double as vowel letters in Syriac generally, not the per-position frequencies this spec uses, which are measured on the shipped gold and cited as such below. Sections 15 and 23 (pp. 10, 16-17) are read for the qushshaya/rukkakha pointing system on the six beghadhkephath letters (b g d k p t): a subscript dot marks the soft/spirant reading, a superscript dot the hard/plosive one, hard word-initially and after consonants, soft after any vowel. Section 23 also states that East-Syrian (Nestorian) usage gives pe a hard pronunciation almost throughout, which is the historical antecedent this spec cites for pe not spirantizing in the modern dialect. The majliana mark (gamal/kaph/zain/shin as affricates) is a later East-Syriac reading-tradition sign and does not appear in this grammar; that claim is not sourced from this work.

wikipron.measured: None of the 7851 gold headwords in aii_syrc_narrow.tsv carry any Syriac combining diacritic (vowel points or qushshaya/rukkakha/majliana dots): the gold is entirely unpointed East Syriac. The residual after the real spec is dominated by the hypothesis omitting phones the gold writes but the unpointed script never encodes (leading deletions: a 2244, length mark 1578, short vowels), not by choosing the wrong reading among written alternatives (begadkepat-direction mismatches total only 440, an order of magnitude smaller).
